primary_sources: Robert H. Clancy, Congressional Record, 68th Congress, 1st Session, 1924

stimulus.text: Paraphrase of Representative Robert H. Clancy, speaking in the House of Representatives in 1924 against the immigration bill: Clancy said that newcomers had always faced bitter complaints, from the Irish and Germans of the 1840s to the Italians, Poles, Jews, Greeks, and Russians of his own day. He called the bill's use of the 1890 census “racial discrimination at its worst,” a deliberate attempt to aim a blow at the peoples of eastern and southern Europe.
stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of Robert H. Clancy, Congressional Record, 68th Congress, 1st Session, 1924 (public domain, U.S. government). The quoted phrase “racial discrimination at its worst” is Clancy's own wording.

source: original; stimulus paraphrased from Robert H. Clancy, Congressional Record, 1924, public domain
stem: Clancy's main argument against the immigration bill was that it

options.text: let too many immigrants enter the country
options.misconception: Clancy defended immigrants against the bill. He wanted fewer limits, not tighter ones.

options.text: singled out eastern and southern Europeans by design
gave too much power to the president
options.misconception: Clancy never mentions the president's power. His complaint is about how the bill picks its targets.

options.text: ignored the needs of American workers
options.misconception: Clancy argues about fairness to newcomers, not about jobs. Workers' needs never enter his speech.

rationales.A: Clancy defended immigrants against the bill. He wanted fewer limits, not tighter ones.
rationales.B: Clancy says the bill goes back to the 1890 census on purpose, so that it aims a blow at eastern and southern Europeans. The discrimination is the design, not an accident.
rationales.C: Clancy never mentions the president's power. His complaint is about how the bill picks its targets.
rationales.D: Clancy argues about fairness to newcomers, not about jobs. Workers' needs never enter his speech.
rationales.general:
1. Find Clancy's charge: the bill is 'racial discrimination at its worst.'
2. Find his evidence: the bill reaches back to the 1890 census.
3. Ask why that year matters: it counts groups before the newer waves arrived.
4. Name the argument: the bill was built to hit eastern and southern Europeans.
Remember: when a speaker names the year a law uses, ask who that year leaves out.
